examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Build control outputs from opcode, timing state and status flags. A hardwired controller is a finite-state circuit whose next-state/output logic implements the micro-operations. Count the actual states and control bits needed by the design; hardwired does not imply every instruction completes in one cycle.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A controller has 13 distinct control states encoded in binary. What is the minimum number of state flip-flops?

**Answer: 4.** An r-bit state register encodes at most 2ʳ states. Three bits give only 8, while four give 16. Thus ceil(log₂13)=4 flip-flops suffice, leaving three unused encodings.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Unused state encodings still need a defined recovery/reset policy in a robust hardware design. Binary and one-hot state encodings have different flip-flop counts.

A datapath’s physical connections limit what a control word can legally request in one cycle.
